column5: Instances of E41 Appellation do not identify things by their meaning, even if they happen to have one, but instead by convention, tradition, or agreement. A given instance of E41 Appellation can have alternative forms, i.e., other instances of E41 Appellation that are always regarded as equivalent independent from the thing it denotes. column22:
This class comprises abstract temporal extents, in the sense of Galilean physics, having a beginning, an end and a duration. 
 
Time Span has no other semantic connotations. Time-Spans are used to define the temporal extent of instances of E4 Period, E5 Event and any other phenomena valid for a certain time. An E52 Time-Span may be identified by one or more instances of E49 Time Appellation. 
 
Since our knowledge of history is imperfect, instances of E52 Time-Span can best be considered as approximations of the actual Time-Spans of temporal entities. The properties of E52 Time-Span are intended to allow these approximations to be expressed precisely.  An extreme case of approximation, might, for example, define an E52 Time-Span having unknown beginning, end and duration. Used as a common E52 Time-Span for two events, it would nevertheless define them as being simultaneous, even if nothing else was known. (Definition of the CIDOC Conceptual Reference Model version 6.2)
 
Automatic processing and querying of instances of E52 Time-Span is facilitated if data can be parsed into an E61 Time Primitive.
 
Examples:
1961
From 12-17-1993 to 12-8-1996
14h30 – 16h22 4th July 1945
9.30 am 1.1.1999 to 2.00 pm 1.1.1999
duration of the Ming Dynasty

This class comprises people, either individually or in groups, who have the potential to perform intentional actions of kinds for which someone may be held responsible.  (Definition of the CIDOC Conceptual Reference Model version 6.2)
 
The CRM does not attempt to model the inadvertent actions of such actors. Individual people should be documented as instances of E21 Person, whereas groups should be documented as instances of either E74 Group or its subclass E40 Legal Body.
 
Examples:
London and Continental Railways (E40)
the Governor of the Bank of England in 1975 (E21)
Sir Ian McKellan (E21)

column4: A unique MAEASaM identifier (ID) is given to each chronology resource. The ID should be written as follow: CHRN-8 digit numeric values.
column5: The name value is the name of the chronology entry.
column6: Name type defines the name as either primary, alternative, local or other and derives from a concept list.
column7: Chronology Type is a field where the defining characteristic of a period or chronological resource entry is specified in simple terms. More than one chronology type can be selected for a chronology resource entry.  In case the defining characteristic of the time period is not clear in the original source (i.e. not stated or undefined) the type “Non-specified” can be used. However, this is best avoided. MAEASaM has compiled 8 broad chronology types each of which may contain subgroupings; these include 1. Geological Timescale, 2. Archaeological Period, 3.  Architectural style, 4. Local sequence, 5. Material culture, 6.Oral or documented marker, 7. Polity, and 8. Palaeoclimate or palaeoenvironmental reconstruction. The description of each concept may be used as a guide for the general characteristics from which the chronology resource entry has been determined.  Multiple chronology types can be used.
column8: A particular geographical area defined by the cardinal points in terms of East, West, South, Central and North Africa, or part of a state, country, or district or local area. The MAEASaM regional chronology has been broadly developed based on the 6 regions described by the African Union  (source: https://www.oecd.org/swac/maps/48-six-regions-African-Union.pdf .
column9: The node records the spatial geometry of the known distribution of the chronological term as a polygon or multi-polygon. The geometry is recorded in Well Known Text (WKT) format.
column10: The node refers to the earliest known occurence of  the period. The date must be reported using the  Extended Date/Time format (EDTF). https://www.loc.gov/standards/datetime/  . Where multiple dates are reported for the same period in the same geographic region, then the earliest date reported should be entered for this node.
column11: The node refers to the latest or most current occurence of the period. The date must be reported using the Extended Date/Time format (EDTF) https://www.loc.gov/standards/datetime/ . Where multiple end dates are reported for the same period in the same geographic region, then the latest date reported should be entered into this node.
column12: The descriptive start date reports on the original date that was converted to the EDTF.
column13: This node uses a concept list to describe the calendrical system that the original start date was reported in before being converted to EDTF.
column14: The descriptive end date reports on the original date that was converted to the EDTF.
column15: This node uses a concept list to describe the calendrical system that the original end date was reported in before being converted to EDTF.
column16: The node requires text entry of the definition and/or defining characteristics of the period. When the text has been directly extracted from the source then the author name, date of publication and page number need to be provided at the end of the definition.
column18: The node refers to how the definition, geometry and/or start and end dates were modified for entry. Examples include: Modification of definition or description: entry was adapted after GETTY AAT (include URL link). Modification of Geometry (Location): Spatial extent modified from Lane, P. 2013 The Archaeology of Pastoralism and Stock keeping in East Africa; In: Oxford Handbook of African Archaeology, Eds Peter Mitchell and Paul Lane, OUP; Causey; Spatial extent not reported. Modification of Start or End Date: start date calibrated (SHC20) at 2 sigma, 98% probability (enter the range) with original date reported 1980±50 (PTA-1100), charcoal, Pit 3, from the site, Toteng, Botswana. Alternative Dates: list of dates and source. Modifications made by recorder (Metadata entry history): indication of what has been modified in the entry with a date (follow EDTF standard for date in string for consistency).
column19: The node is related to the Information Resource Model containing original source information (i.e. publications) from where the chronology resource is derived. Multiple sources may be used.
column20: The node refers to the persistent identifier from where the original term has been used. The node only captures this information when an online thesauri (i.e. Getty AAT, ChronOntology) has been used to create the resource.
column21: Relationship type refers to the connections between related chronology resources. This is described using a controlled vocabulary list.
column22: The node refers to a relationship created with another connected Chronology resource. The unique MAEASaM ID for the related resource will be entered into this node.
column23: The date at which the chronological resource is entered into the database. The date should follow the Extended Date/Time Format https://www.loc.gov/standards/datetime/
column24: The date at which the chronological resource is modified. The date should follow the Extended Date/Time Format https://www.loc.gov/standards/datetime/

column26: This node records the names of the nodes that were modified during an update of the resource record.
